title: IdP compatibility runbook: attribute mappings, fallback flows, and verification checklist
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This ticket produces an IdP-specific compatibility runbook and verification checklist for Redwood Inference SSO (SAML) integrations. The goal is to consolidate non-obvious IdP behaviors (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping), map attribute naming differences into our RBAC v2 rules, document audit capture points, and define safe fallback/rollback flows for admin controls. This runbook will be used by on-call, SEs performing enterprise onboarding, and the Docs/Support teams for troubleshooting.
motivation: Over the past 12 months we’ve seen multiple onboarding and incident cases where subtle IdP differences (NameID formats, groups claim placement, certificate rotation cadence) caused auth failures or incorrect role assignments. This leads to customer downtime and manual remediation. A single, practical runbook that includes test vectors and post-install checks will reduce onboarding friction and incident MTTR.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated IdP compatibility table describing at least: NameID forms, common attribute names (email, uid, userPrincipalName), groups mapping, assertion size/encoding issues, and metadata endpoints for Okta/Azure/GWorkspace/Ping.

A step-by-step verification checklist that SEs can follow to validate successful SAML onboarding (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, certificate rotation test, clock-skew tolerance test, group sync verification).

RBAC v2 mapping examples for 4 common patterns: email-based, username-based, groups claim (array), SCIM-backed group sync. Each example includes example SAML assertion snippets and resulting RBAC role assignment expectations.

Audit logging spec: exact fields captured for every SSO event (assertion_id, issuer, NameID, mapped_principal, mapping_rule_id, outcome, timestamp, raw_assertion_digest) and sample query examples for the Console.
Console UX requirements for exposing mapping warnings/errors to admins when nonstandard attributes are encountered.
A small internal test harness (bash/python) that can generate real SAML responses for end-to-end validation, with usage notes and a GitHub PR reference.
Runbook published to Confluence and linked in the public support KB; internal training session scheduled and recorded for SE/Support teams.
tasks: Inventory IdP quirks: collect posts/contacts and previous incident notes for Okta/Azure/Google/Ping.
Draft mapping table and canonical examples for each IdP.
Create verification checklist and canonical SAML assertion examples (sanitized) to include in docs.
Define audit log schema and add telemetry events to developer spec for runtime instrumentation.
Implement minimal console warnings for attribute mismatches and a link to recommended mappings.
Create test harness repo and open an internal GitHub PR that seeds the repo with examples.
Run canary with three pilot customers and collect feedback; adjust docs/console UX accordingly.
Schedule internal training and add runbook to on-call rotation playbooks.
notes: Design trade-offs discussed 2026-03-04: whether to normalize attributes at ingestion (server-side) or require explicit admin mapping in Console. We decided to implement server-side intelligent defaults + persist explicit mapping to customer config to avoid surprises during certificate rotations.

Edge case: Azure AD sometimes emits userPrincipalName instead of mail; Okta can place groups in an attribute named 'groups' or in a claim named 'okta_groups' depending on directory setup — include both in table.
Clock skew tolerance currently 5 minutes; we will add a diagnostic that checks SP and IdP time offsets and surface a recommended remediation step.
We observed SAML response size limits with large group lists (>20k) for some IdPs — recommend SCIM group sync for orgs with large group counts and include a migration checklist.

implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize compatibility table and verification checklist; ship Confluence draft.
Week 2: implement audit log event spec and wire minimal telemetry in staging; build console warning surface for mapping mismatches.
Week 3: publish test harness and run 3 pilot onboards; collect metrics (auth success rate, mapping warnings, incidents).
Week 4: incorporate feedback, finalize docs, schedule cross-team training, and promote to release branch.
rollback_plan: If console warnings cause UI regressions, toggle the warning feature flag off and deploy a UI patch within the same day.
If audit log volume exceeds quota, disable verbose assertion digest logging via runtime flag and fallback to sampling mode; notify SRE and customers impacted.
If any canary pilot shows incorrect RBAC assignments, revert mapping defaults and require explicit admin mapping while we patch server-side heuristics.
